ledger.note: c. 960: Otto I sets up the Eastern March (Ostarrichi) below the Enns as a Bavarian march. 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave' (some sources give 970, the infobox c. 970); the Lechfeld victory of 955 had begun the reconquest; the page calls it the Bavarian Eastern March. eu-08-a's Kingdom of Germany dossier records the same growth for 960; Austria is drawn as the vassal tint until 1156. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review): the tint is the Enns-Wienerwald strip only ('between the river Enns and the Vienna Woods'); the Vienna basin and the rest of Lower Austria follow the Austria dossier's later gains (1043, 1055) and are tinted from those years. Before 970: the March of Styria exists as a march of Bavaria. 'Created sometime before 970, it was broken off the larger March of Carinthia, itself a march of the Duchy of Bavaria.' 976: Otto II cuts the Duchy of Carinthia out of Bavaria. 'It was separated from the Duchy of Bavaria in 976, and was the first newly created Imperial State'; Henry II, deposed in 974 for revolt, loses the duchy and Henry the Younger is installed.

976: the march leaves Bavaria. 'In 976, it was transferred to the jurisdiction of the newly created Duchy of Carinthia.' The Carinthian side (duchy-of-carinthia 976 vassal_start) and march-of-styria carry the continuation. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking).
1061: Agnes of Poitou enfeoffs Otto of Nordheim with the duchy; the Salian regency replaces the Ottonians' line.
1070: Henry IV establishes Welf rule over Bavaria; the Welf dukes hold it, with breaks, to 1180.

1139: Leopold IV, a Babenberg, is given Bavaria after Henry the Proud is dispossessed in 1138. 'In 1139, Leopold IV inherited Bavaria' (Margraviate of Austria page); Henry Jasomirgott held it from 1141.

ledger.note: 1156: Austria is raised to a duchy independent of Bavaria. 'issued by Holy Roman Emperor Frederick Barbarossa on 17 September 1156': Austria, 'a Bavarian frontier march', becomes an inheritable fief of the Babenbergs; the page names no counties, so the Land below the Enns is the researcher's reading. Repair of 2026-10-25: the mirror vassal_end is in margraviate-of-austria; the region is the whole march as it stood in 1156.
1156: Henry the Lion regains Bavaria as a 'diminished' duchy when the Babenbergs renounce it at the Regensburg diet of 8 September 1156.

1180: Otto of Wittelsbach becomes duke of Bavaria. 'He was finally rewarded with the duchy of Bavaria on 16 September 1180 at Altenburg in Thuringia' after Henry the Lion's deposition; the Wittelsbach line holds Bavaria to 1918. Same year: Styria is raised to a duchy ('With the separation of Styria under Duke Ottokar IV in the same year, Bavaria lost the last of her southeastern territories', Otto I page; 'raised to the Duchy of Styria in 1180', Duchy of Bavaria page). Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking): this is now a caption only. The earlier 1180 loss to duchy-of-styria is dropped because no Bavarian keyframe ever drew Styria after 976 and duchy-of-styria (eu-09) is founded from march-of-styria, not from Bavaria; Styria's Bavarian years (before 970 to 976) are the vassal pair below.

notes:
Six pages opened (budget 2-5; the sixth, Margraviate of Austria, was opened for the Austria dossier and is cited here for the Eastern March). Cliopatria has no stem-duchy row; Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria starts 1260 (eu-09). Not settled: (a) Styria 976-1180: the Bavaria and Otto I pages say it was separated from Bavaria in 1180, the Carinthia and March of Styria pages put it under Carinthia from 976, so the shape leaves it out and the 1180 loss is a caption (confidence 2); (b) the extent of the March of Verona (see march-of-verona); (c) the Duchy of Bavaria page gives no area and no complete list of dukes (the extraction gave only appointment years), so no ruler strip is given; (d) 1255-1259 are drawn by no Cliopatria row; (e) Carinthia joined Bavaria in 911 (Bavaria page) or 889 (Carinthia page). The Henry the Lion personal union 1156-1180 is in stem-duchy-of-saxony. The Eastern March (c. 960-1155, margraviate-of-austria), the March of Verona (952-975, march-of-verona) and Carinthia (to 976, duchy-of-carinthia) are separate dossiers written in this batch; Styria, now clarified by the March of Styria page (under Carinthia from 976), is march-of-styria. Counterparts needing dossiers: duchy-of-lower-bavaria. Gazetteer lacks Landshut and Burghausen (coordinates used).

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (1) Bavaria is now Bayern minus Franconia (the gazetteer circles, with the Nordgau polygon kept) and minus a polygon west of the Lech; the Duchy of Bavaria page was re-read for this (duchy 'without its Swabian and Franconian regions', Nordgau included; the page is silent on a western boundary at the Lech, which comes from the Duchy of Swabia page: 'to the right bank of the river Lech'). (2) Salzburg: 1213 loss to prince-archbishopric-of-salzburg and the 976 keyframe split at 1213; the Salzburg page puts full independence from the Bavarian dukes in the late 13th century, so the loss is soft. (3) Styria: the 1180 loss is dropped (caption only in the 1180 rename); the vassal pair 970-976 with march-of-styria replaces it. (4) Austria: the 960 vassal tint is the Enns-Wienerwald strip only; the mirrors are added in margraviate-of-austria and march-of-verona. (4b) The Swabia dossier's region (an 80 km circle round Augsburg, which reached Munich) was trimmed in the same repair to Bayern west of the same Lech polygon, so the two dossiers meet on one line with no overlap; the gazetteer's Franconia circles (Nuremberg 90 km) still reach into the Nordgau, so stem-duchy-of-franconia (906-939, pass, not touched) overlaps this shape by about 30 cells in 907-938. (5) Thin finding: the Brixen page dates immediacy 1027 (not a detachment from Bavaria) and says nothing of Trent; Tirol stays in the shape; the Traungau is not found on the March of Styria page. (6) Routing: duchy-of-bavaria (eu-09) must start in 1255, not 1260, with stem-duchy-of-bavaria as predecessor; the Franconian lands after 939 and the Allgäu west of the Lech are drawn by nobody in this batch.
